simple.meaning: אוּלַי (ʼûwlay) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “if not ; hence perhaps.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 45 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Joshua, 1 Samuel, and 12 more, beginning at Genesis 16:2. Its contexts include righteousness, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אוּלַי (H194).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: אוּלַי (ʼûwlay) / H194 is traced through Genesis 16:2, Genesis 18:24, Genesis 18:28, Genesis 18:29 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.
definitions.full: H194. ulay II. אוּלַי 44 and ( Gen 24:39 ) אֻלַי adverb (perhaps from אוֺ & לַי = לֵא לֵי, , as in לוּלֵא , = or not ? ). 1 peradventure, perhaps; usually expressing a hope , as Gen 16:2 ; Num 22:6 , 11 ; 23:3 ; 1Sam 6:5 ; Jer 20:10 ; but also a fear or doubt, as Gen 27:12 ; Job 1:5 , followed by לֹא Gen 24:5 , 39 ; in mockery Isa 47:12 ; Jer 51:8 . 2 followed by another clause ἀσυνδέτως , it, it expresses vir-tually the protasis = if peradventure Gen 18:24 , 28 (compare 18:29-32 ) Hosea 8:7 the blade shall yield no meal; יִבְלָעֻהוּ זָרִים יַעֲשֶׂה אוּלַי if perchance it yield, strangers shall swallow it up. 3 in Num 22:33 לוּלֵי (q.v) must be read; unless she had turned aside from me, surely, etc.
